text: Attended eye clinic here. Very busy hospital, but very efficient, capable and caring staff. Staff spoke reasonable English and were so helpful. Very well equipped clinic with latest equipment. I have been to private hospitals in Thailand, which are really great, but for value and to support the public health system, I will return here for sure. The cost for the consult with medicine included was less than the cost for the medicine alone back home. You can have great confidence in the care and skill at this hospital.

I went to visit a friend of mine after a terrible motorcycle accident. I visited him after a rather complicated surgery. The room assigned to him looks like a high-end hotel with all the comforts. He has to sleep on a bed that can be adjusted to a 90° angle to avoid straining his breathing. The hospital is better equipped than any in Europe. The nursing staff is kind, knowledgeable, and speaks English. High standard.
Thank you for take care my friend.

As a foreigner living in Thailand since 5 years, paying my tax and social security I am entitled to use this hospital for a very affordable rate. It's very sad to see many bad comments about this place. The staff are very attentive, helpful and really doing their best. Yes they are busy and it makes a rush environment but nothing diferente from a public hospital in Europe or south America (where I lived from many years).  At the least here they still smelling and are kind. Thank you to many staff, nurse and doctor at Vachira hospital, keep doing your professional job as I saw today. ❤️ 🙏

The main hospital in Phuket.

It is typical government hospital. It will take hours waiting before seeing a doctor. Some staffs are really helpful but some are terrible.

Tips: avoid an old nurse lady.  They always are aggressive. They yell at everybody even an innocent old patient (I saw it happens very often)

Because ton of people go there every day so doctor need to diagnose very fast. Sometimes, it seems that they see nothing and then give you medicine. Not even touch. Like a magic 🦄🧙

They now have a new building for foreigners. It is better to go there directly because most staffs cannot speak English very well.

If you're in the hospital and need a place for prayer, proceed to the second floor by the stairs/ramp near the international customer service area. Pass the convenient store and around the corner from Cafe Amazon, you will find the Muslim prayer room. It's equipped with a wudu (ablution) area and also includes a section for women. Qibla direction is marked on the ceiling. Alhamdulillah for this facility.

I had the worst experience at this hospital in Phuket. I arrived on my own, in a critical condition with a racing heartbeat, dizziness, and I even collapsed in the street before getting there. I felt like I was about to die but nobody seemed to care. The very first thing they did was ask for my passport at such a difficult moment.

After some time, they finally took me to the observation area, threw me on a bed, and completely ignored me. No one spoke to me, no one checked on me, and when I tried to ask something, they either didn’t answer or replied in a rude, dismissive way.

If this was a foreigner in my country (Kuwait) in such a condition, they would have been treated immediately with respect and proper care. I’m extremely disappointed with how I was treated here.

To be fair, there was one doctor I don’t remember his name who was very kind, reassuring, and respectful. He was neither thin nor heavyset, and he truly stood out as the only compassionate person I encountered. But the rest of the staff? Completely uninterested, even if I had died there.

Arrived by motorcycle at 8.15 am. NOWHERE to park. Had to park 200 metres away. God only knows what car drivers do ! Or people with limited mobility.  I guess they have to rely on other people to drive them.
By the time I was seen by a doctor after approximately 2 hours,  I had to wait in no fewer than 5 queues. Then another for the cashier which snaked into the adjoining room. And then an ever longer wait for my medicine. 7 queues in total.
The instructions of where to go were very vague. The staff were not very helpful. The female doctor however was very nice and the costs were very reasonable.  B300 for the consultation and B105 for 2 medications.
So a mixed bag , but leaning towards a negative experience.

Was referred here by mission hospital for urgent specialist care/test regarding terminal condition. Admin staff were helpful and doctor was both professional and proficient in English.

Foreigners have a dedicated counter upon arrival.

8 dec 23. Come here because have SSO card and need sick leave. Cough, running nose, fever. At first, it is really hard to park vehicle and navigate. Find international service information, they send to counter 33, which was closed. When open, they look at my card, ask what I want and send to registration number 8. Register n.8 send to register number 1, which was busy and finally registered at number 2. She send to counter 24, and nurse there said that quew at 13.00 is full already (time was 13.10) and they will start accepted cases again at 17:00. Because they have only one doctor who work. But have five nurses who literally have nothing to do. Any large amount of sick people who come to see doctor and can not. Maybe if there be 5 doctors in 5 examination rooms there be good service, but right now hospital save money for doctors and spend it for nurse. If you have choice and pay by yourself, there is better option on Phuket who can care better.

After waiting for nothing for two hours, screening nurse ask for chief complaints and send to Ari clinic, which is another department. Lovely)))

My father did his chemo therapy here and the most recent time he vomited for 2 hours straight the nurses in the chemo room didn’t do anything and just left him to vomit in the toilet. I came a little later when my dad has just finished vomitting he has sat down sweating and pale so I asked if he needed water which he did but isn’t this the nurses job? And also with the cashier I wanted a break through of all the costs and I asked for a bill for every cycle my dad has done and the cashier gave me attitude and wasn’t very nice. I had an appointment to see the doctor at 4pm, but it's now 7pm and the doctor still hasn't arrived. Many people have been waiting for three hours. What is the doctor doing? Communication and no organization with the patient and between the workers.

When we payed them the bill they waited inpatient to get the money in their hands

We left on own decision the place and then one day later went to a private hospital (modern technology, good nurses and doctors, rooms f the patient)

I was the only foreigner in a ward of over 30 Thai people, however they all greeted me and made me feel very welcome. I love Thai people, genuinely nice and helpful and had some good conversations and made some friends.

It may not be the most advanced hospital in the world, but the people are what made my experience a good one.

My wife gets an emergency condition, so we have to bring her by the ambulance to emergency room . Unfortunately the ambulance brings us to this hospital. I don’t know what’s the policy and procedure in Thailand hospitals , but this is the …

Unfriendly,  unwilling and uncompasioate.

My mother passed away and was transported here, I asked to see her body as soon as I arrived as I flew in to Phuket from Rayong.
I was told I could not see her until the doctor arrived again next Tuesday..
Once the doctor arrived I learned that no preparation had been done and the body had just been sat in the refrigerator for the past 4 days...so what would the difference have been seeing her Saturday? It would have helped ease my pain seeing her but instead I suffered all weekend wanting to let her know I was there.

When asking the unfriendly manager downstairs in the international department , all I recived were cold uncaring answers. Really could not have been any less compassionate and understanding than that woman.

Once transporting my mother's body out of the hospital, the mortuary staff carrying her were laughing and joking around whilst I watched my mother's corpse loading into the back of a truck. I know it is not there mother and they are not grieving but they could at lease have the courtesy to show a small amount of respect...
From what was already the most painful experience I have had in my life and still going through, I can say this hospital did nothing in any way to make thing easier and more comfortable for me.
Absolute discrace.

I hope you never have to go through what you put me through

Got here with an eye infection. At first its confusing, but once u understand the system its ok. The doctors are really profesional. Would say even better than in my country. U get the medicine from pharmacy downstairs afterwards. Was done in 3 hours. Better come at 8 before opening..

text: If you are a foreigner, do yourself a favor and do not come here. This place is disorganized and no one here speaks English well. I needed to get 4 stitches removed. For the first 2.5 hours, they shifted me around to several different stations - general history check, orthopedic, general surgery, and had me wait around in each of the queues for a very long time before telling me I needed to be somewhere else. They eventually get me into a line called “dressing room” and say the wait is at least an hour. I ended up leaving and having my husband cut off the stitches at the pharmacy cross the street with hydrogen peroxide, alcohol, scissors, and tweezers he bought there.

Go to a different hospital.

If you can just go to a different hospital. The experience I had was ridiculous. …

While on holiday, my mum was rushed here in critical condition for emergency treatment. Initially I was skeptical and the language barrier made me more anxious but as I observed their actions in the emergency room, I realized they were doing their very best, to a remarkable standard. They stabilized my mum within an hour, and she was put under observation for a week. The hospital and the general ward aren't luxurious, but were comfortable enough, and our main concern was quality medical care, which she got. The nurses and doctors were meticulous about every detail that was contributing to her condition, and periodically checked on her every hour, sometimes more when there was an issue. I've seen some negative comments about the politeness of staff but I disagree, the one thing that made our week here bearable was the warmth and care that the nurses gave my mum, and the patience with which they showed us how to help in caregiving. There were always some nurses that knew some English and were able to communicate with us effectively. Even the insurance department were patient with us when our insurance company were taking long to respond to the claim. All in all, I would definitely place my faith in this hospital, from my experience

Then wanted all his medical insurance information. I called regularly asking if he was awake and they told me he was on a ventilator and couldn't talk. Even after a week. The hospital lied and kept him looking for insurance money. If the embassy wouldn't of checked on him he would of been in trouble. text: This is a large, well-equipped hospital. The assistance provided to foreign tourists is very well organized. Staff members dedicated to working with foreigners helped us with everything. We were impressed by their work! They are very friendly and caring. They have a challenging job, yet they are true professionals. I can't imagine how we would have managed without them. Their names are Patcharin Singbuppa and Kruapha Phahonkan. I would love for the management to recognize these employees; they go above and beyond their duties.

I used the services at the Mahogany Building. The service wasn't very fast, but the medical history taking was quite thorough, checking the patient's information and name every time. Dr. Sarayut in the Obstetrics department was very thorough and kind to patients. Overall, it was quite good.

On Tuesday, I went to get a queue number at 4:00 AM and got a slot at 4:30 AM. I registered at 5:00 AM to see a specialist. However, when it was my turn, the nurse informed me that I had previously been seen by Doctor A and suggested I come back on Monday because Doctor A wasn't there that day; only Doctors B and C were available. She said that if I saw another doctor, they would refer me back to Doctor A because he/she had seen me before, and Doctor B and C already had patients. I was there because I was sick, but my usual doctor wasn't available. Couldn't another doctor treat or advise me instead? I wasn't aware of this situation beforehand. The hospital's system is convenient for both staff and doctors, but the patient management system is never convenient. Doctors can change their appointment days without asking if it's convenient for the patient, but patients have no choice; they have to follow the doctor's instructions. I tried to follow all the procedures, but the system didn't facilitate anything. In the end, I couldn't see my doctor because he/she wasn't available, and I have to come back on Monday. The nurse did the best she could by issuing an appointment slip. Please improve your system, as accessing specialists in each department is difficult for patients.

The service was awful. When I asked a question, they said they didn't know. How would people coming to see a doctor know? It was so confusing. This was at the Outpatient Department, Internal Medicine, 2nd floor, counter 19. The staff member assisting the patients was overweight, dark-skinned, had straightened hair, and no hair net. Her service was terrible. I'm so confused because I work in the hospital profession too, and I've never seen other patients treated like this. Is it just their personality? Or do they think they can be rude just because they're out of uniform? Other patient assistants in uniform treat you like family. I should bring my Vachira Hospital staff badge here too. If you provide this kind of service, you shouldn't be working in customer service. I feel sorry for the patients. (Appointment slip issuer, counter 19, morning shift, June 30th, 2026)

I was admitted to this hospital in May 2026 for surgery on a fractured hand and stayed for 3 nights and 4 days. Afterward, I requested my medical records to use in my personal accident insurance claim. Now, almost a month later, I've called the medical records department to follow up and was told that the documents are being compiled for the director's approval. I want to review the service as extremely slow; the documents haven't even been processed yet, and the processing fees are very expensive compared to the service. I'm writing this review because I've already submitted my insurance claim, but I'm missing my medical records, which are delayed, and I've received a letter from the insurance company requesting them, valid for only 15 days after receipt.

P.S. Compared to other government hospitals where I stayed for 2 months and also requested medical records for insurance claims, I received them within 2 weeks. Here, after only 3 nights and 4 days of stay, the process is significantly slower. This feedback is for improvement. The wait is extremely long.

This doesn't even include... Some departments have very slow working hours. At lunchtime, the lights are turned off, the counters are closed, and work starts very late. For example, in the morning, staff start work at 8:30 AM. There should be staff to rotate shifts; this isn't a corporate job, this is a service industry. Especially in a government hospital with naturally high patient numbers, staff work only 8:30 AM - 12:00 PM and 1:00 PM - 2:00 PM. While I understand staff are human beings, there should be more shifts and rotating staff to increase work hours.

I appreciate the doctors and nurses; they do a good job, provide good treatment, and speak politely. However, general staff who aren't doctors, nurses, or patient assistants in other departments are treated very poorly, often disrespectfully. Sometimes, patients understand that they might prefer convenient and nearby treatment, but once treatment begins, they want it to be completed satisfactorily. There's nothing wrong with the treatment itself, but the after-treatment service, including paperwork and reception, is not good.
The wait was very long. You won't get medicine unless you ask. If your symptoms are severe, I think you shouldn't come.

Today, Thursday, April 30, 2026, I received services at Vajira Hospital and had a negative experience with a nurse at counter 34 on the first floor, at the patient registration counter. I won't try to name the nurse at the counter, but I know you probably know who it was at the time and date I mentioned above.
On that day, I had appointments with two doctors around the same time, so I had to spend almost the entire day at the hospital. Towards the end of my visit (around 4:30 PM), I was quite confused about the procedure, as it was my first time submitting documents for a referral to a hospital in another province. So I went to ask for information at the counter on the first floor (counter number 34), trying to ask the nurse there, who hadn't yet posted a "closed" sign, or perhaps because it wasn't past closing time yet, but there were no other patients waiting and registering around me that I could see. I tried to ask for information and called out to her several times, but received no response. The nurse was using her mobile phone, stretching and lying down on her chair while working, and not paying attention to the patients. However, there was another nurse... I was sitting at counter number 55 when a staff member came to my aid and provided appropriate information, for which I would like to express my sincere gratitude 🙏🏼. Based on this experience, I would like to suggest that the hospital consider improving both the clarity of procedures provided to patients and the service standards of its staff. This is to ensure that patients receive appropriate convenience and care, especially during times when they may be confused or anxious. Please improve your service standards, as every patient deserves proper care and attention, particularly in a place that requires trust and confidence like this.

In April 2026, I was admitted to the women's surgical ward twice because I needed two surgeries. This was the first time in my life I had to wait for surgery at a public hospital.

The nurses were lovely. Many spoke politely and smiled, although some had serious expressions or seemed a bit stern. I understand they must have been very tired, but I also understand the patients' perspective. The pain from the wound makes us emotionally vulnerable. Sometimes, a nurse raising their voice could upset some patients. I understand all sides, but I can assure you that all the nurses tried their best to help the patients.

Thank you to the doctors, nurses, and staff who cared for me throughout my admission. Now I will try my best to prevent the wound from getting infected again so I don't have to bother them again.
